technology_name: Cryopreservation Protocol for Pollen and Spores
institution: KSCSTE- Malabar Botanical Garden & Institute for Plant Sciences (MBGIPS)
problem_solved: Securing the long-term viability, genetic stability, and sustainable sourcing of high-value plant species.
description: A cryopreservation protocol developed to secure the long-term viability of pollen and spores from high-value plant species, ensuring genetic stability and successful post-thaw recovery. The protocol covers medicinal, ornamental, and ecologically important plants, including ferns (e.g., Asplenium nidus), angiosperms (e.g., Clitoria ternatea), Nymphaea, Crinum, Costus, and orchid varieties. It supports the sustainable sourcing of elite planting materials, providing consistent inputs for the herbal, pharmaceutical, and floriculture sectors.
applications:
• Sustainable sourcing of elite planting material for pharmaceutical and herbal sectors

• Consistent, high-quality inputs for the wellness and antioxidant-rich food industries

• Supply of cryo-banked ornamental plants (Nymphaea, orchids, ferns) for the floriculture market

• Long-term biodiversity conservation and genetic banking of high-value plant species
contact_person: Dr. Manjula K M & Dr. N S Pradeep
secondary_sector: Biotechnology & Life Sciences, MedTech & Health Care, Agribusiness & Rural Economy
